summary: Configured sudo command logging on node1 to /var/log/sudo-commands.log (with user, host, and timestamp per entry) while suppressing those entries from the general system log (auth.log/journal), via a validated /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging drop-in. Performed the mandatory single-node restart with proof of a changed boot identity and confirmed the logging configuration and behavior persisted after reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/sudo version and existing sudo/syslog setup (cmd-c47cc3e21b5b40c2)

Created /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging with Defaults logfile=/var/log/sudo-commands.log, log_year/log_host, and !syslog; validated with visudo -cf; pre-created log file with 0600 root:root perms; ran test sudo commands and confirmed entries in sudo-commands.log with no COMMAND= leakage into auth.log/journal (cmd-b7564bfa4eb04093)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, sudoers file content, log file perms/line count (cmd-8f726ee93e564311)
Issued background-delayed systemctl reboot so the exec acknowledgement returned before disconnection (cmd-2bd4cb4294ee4bd7)
Polled node1 until it became unreachable then reachable again (cmd-e1cce210f22a4989, cmd-fac369ccef904320, cmd-0f03f07678be4483)
Verified new boot_id differs from baseline, proving an actual restart occurred

Post-restart verification: sudoers file intact and valid, log file present, new sudo command logged correctly, no COMMAND= leakage in auth.log or this boot's journal since the config was applied (cmd-ba5312a62b7b4711, cmd-cdc73656b6164091)

evidence.requirement: Every sudo command is recorded with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: sudo-commands.log entries show format 'TIMESTAMP : user : HOST=node1 ... USER=root ; COMMAND=...' both before and after the reboot

evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: After applying Defaults !syslog, no new COMMAND= lines appear in /var/log/auth.log or the journal; grep of auth.log shows the only COMMAND= matches predate the config change at 09:16:16, and journalctl -b for the post-reboot boot shows zero COMMAND= entries

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart with proof of changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b185f188-42be-40d1-84ea-f7c9a76f5c8d captured, reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect, node briefly unreachable, then came back with new boot_id 85b662c9-2240-4412-963e-20ae03173743
After reboot, /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging still parses OK via visudo, log file persists, and a fresh sudo command correctly appends to sudo-commands.log with no leakage elsewhere
